chunks: Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from al-Halabi said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about one who did not catch the Friday sermon, so he said: 'He prays two rak'ahs. And if the prayer was missed for him so he did not catch it, let him pray four.' And he said: 'If you catch the Imam before he bows in the last rak'ah, you have caught the prayer. And if you catch him after he has bowed, it is Dhuhr (four rak'ahs).'

key_terms.اَلْجُمُعَة: Friday (specifically referring to the congregational prayer)
key_terms.اَلْخُطْبَة: The sermon delivered before the Friday prayer

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings for Friday prayer if one misses the sermon or arrives late?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between missing the Friday sermon (Khutbah) versus missing the prayer unit (Salat) itself, a key topic in Shia fiqh. It establishes that catching the Imam’s bowing (Ruku') in the final rak'ah is sufficient to count the prayer as Friday, whereas arriving after it reverts it to Dhuhr, reflecting the principle of 'catching the prayer' rather than just the Imam. This ruling underscores the importance of timely participation in communal worship while providing practical flexibility for latecomers.
